name: Patch kits
blurb: Planks cut to size, oakum and a pot of pitch: four kits to stop a leak at sea.

name: Mend kits
blurb: Canvas cut into patches, twine and spare line: three kits to mend torn rigging at sea.

name: Crates
blurb: A load of lumber knocked into four plain crates.

name: False-light rig
blurb: A lantern on a pole with colored glass, kerosene for a night's burning.

name: Repair stores
blurb: Lockers built in under the cabin sole: room for four more of each kit. Install it at a slipway.

name: Powder and shot
blurb: Scrap iron cast into ball and cut into chain and grape, made up in cartridges: a keg of ten charges, for any kind you fire.

name: Lockpicks
blurb: Spring steel filed into six picks and a tension wrench.

name: Crowbars
blurb: Two pry bars drawn out of bar iron on the anvil.

name: Improved carriages
blurb: Iron-shod carriages with better tackle: the guns reload a fifth faster. Install them at a slipway.

name: Barrels
blurb: Staves split and hooped into eight tight barrels.

name: Salt fish
blurb: Fresh fish split, salted down and packed in barrels: it keeps all winter.

name: Re-crate stolen goods
blurb: A load of hot goods unpacked and packed again in a plain crate: the company's marks are gone, though the theft is still remembered.

name: Untaxed whiskey
blurb: Wheat mashed with well water, run through the still and casked: four loads of whiskey no revenue man has seen. A batch takes a week.

name: Mend kits
blurb: Canvas cut to patterns on the loft floor, with twine, palms and spare line: five kits from a bolt where the bench gets three.

name: Quality canvas
blurb: A new suit of close-woven duck, cut and roped on the loft floor: 5% faster at every sail. Fit it at a slipway.

name: Topsails
blurb: Bigger, lighter gaff topsails and a fisherman staysail between the masts: faster in light and moderate airs at Full, but she shows further and strains sooner in a blow. Fit it at a slipway.

name: Storm sails
blurb: Heavy canvas, double-sewn and roped for the reefed and half sails: they carry 4 knots more wind before the rig strains. Fit it at a slipway.

name: Dark-tanned sails
blurb: A suit of sails soaked in a vat of bark and tar until they're the color of a wet hull: a quarter harder to see in the dark. Fit it at a slipway.

name: Muffled blocks
blurb: Sheaves bushed with leather and the blocks wrapped in served canvas: no creak or clatter for a watchman to hear close in at night. Fit it at a slipway.

name: Smoked fish
blurb: Fresh fish split, brined in well water and hung over a slow hardwood fire for a week, then packed: it keeps as salt fish does, with no salt bought.

name: Smoked venison
blurb: Poached venison cut in strips, salted and hung in the smoke a week: it keeps through the summer, travels light, and nobody can say which island it walked on.

name: Powder and shot by the keg
blurb: Shot cast at the forge, then made up in cartridges here in a lot: four kegs in four hours, where the forge alone takes two hours a keg.

name: Corrected charts
blurb: Your soundings, bearings and the pilots' marks copied fair onto clean sheets: better courses, and chart voyages run 8% faster. Fit it at a slipway; it takes an instruments slot.
